title: Count Pairs of Connectable Servers in a Weighted Tree Network
summary: Given an unrooted weighted tree with n vertices, where each vertex represents a server, and an array of edges with weights, along with a signal speed, determine the number of server pairs connectable through each server.
statement: Given an unrooted weighted tree with n vertices, where each vertex represents a server, and an array of edges with weights, along with a signal speed, determine the number of server pairs connectable through each server. For each server, count pairs (a, b) where a < b, and both paths from the server to a and b are divisible by the signal speed, without sharing edges.
constraints: edges describes a connected weighted tree with vertices 0 through n-1 and positive weights.
For center c, both endpoint distances from c must be divisible by signal_speed and their paths from c must share no edge.
Return the qualifying unordered endpoint-pair count for every possible center.
hints: Removing a center separates the tree into neighbor branches; two paths share no center-adjacent edge exactly when endpoints lie in different branches.
For each center, count speed-divisible distances within each neighbor branch, then combine branch counts pairwise.
DFS each branch with accumulated distance; add earlier_count*current_count and then extend earlier_count.
Each valid pair has one endpoint in each of two unique branches and is counted once when the later branch is combined with all earlier branches.
editorial: Each valid pair has one endpoint in each of two unique branches and is counted once when the later branch is combined with all earlier branches.

tests.explanation: At internal centers, qualifying endpoints from different branches form 4, 6, 6, and 4 pairs; leaves have none.
At center one, servers zero and two are both distance three in different branches, producing one pair.
